newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Teljoy sees full year loss.
newsitem.headline: Teljoy sees full year loss.

text.p: Teljoy Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to incur an attributable loss in the current year but estimated it would be substantially lower than the previous year.
The electronics and mobile phone company said it experienced problems in its television and satellite division services which had now been merged.
"The directors expect the group to incur a loss for the full year but the loss will be substantially lower than the 48.2 million rand loss last year," the group said in a statement.

Teljoy Television services declared an attributable loss of 11.8 million rand for the year ended September 30 compared to a 7.3 million rand profit in the same period last year. The satellite division recorded a loss of 4.6 million rand.

However, the group said the divisional results excluded a capital profit of 13.8 million rand on the sale of a further ten percent of Teljoy Cellular to Vodacom -- the joint venture network operator owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc and state-run Telkom SA. -- for 18.6 million rand.
"Taking this into account, the attributable loss for the period amounted to 8.5 million rand compared to 2.2 million rand in 1995," it said.

"The sale of Teljoy Cellular shares, together with the proceeds of the sale of (cellular subscriber base) Afrilink and the repayment of 38 million rand of debt by Teljoy Cellular to the top company did much to improve group liquidity," the group added.
However, entry into satellite proved expensive for Teljoy Television Services and drew the attention of management away from the core rental business.
This resulted in the debtors book, service levels and productivity deteriorating, leading to costs outstripping revenues.
